items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: the last one I just had was February 26 with Jeff Coffin, a duo, and it’s just the two of us playing saxophone.

ctx.x: Did you ever have the experience playing in combos where you found it dissatisfying. Did that have anything to do with you choosing to be mostly a solo artist?

Yeah. It’s funny. I’m kind of coming around to the other side where my last two albums have now — the last one I just had was February 26 with Jeff Coffin, a duo, and it’s just the two of us playing saxophone. And then the one before that I wrote a big band album and it’s kind of my sound, it’s called “All Figured Out.” And it’s with a complete big band. I wrote all the parts, and it’s called “All Figured Out” as an ironic way of like I don’t know what the heck I’m doing but this is fun for me. And now I’m…

festivals, in Europe. That’s amazing. And people don’t have to know how many emails I sent, how I did it. But man I sure put it on my website, and hey, international musician. And then hopefully, yes, I can’t send 6,000 emails every year, but hopefully it does get a little bit easier and it has, as your name gets out there. But you have to keep doing the work and this industry has a very short attention span. It seems even shorter now with social media where you’ve got to be putting stuff out all the time. But…
